stemMarkdown: A train 285 m long travelling at 69 km/h overtakes a man walking at 6.3 km/h in the same direction as the train. How many seconds does the train take to pass him completely? (Round to 4 decimal places.)
solutionMarkdown: Same direction, so the speeds subtract: $69 - 6.3 = 62.7$ km/h $= 17.4167$ m/s. The train covers its own length relative to the man: $\dfrac{285}{17.4167} = 16.3636$ seconds.
altSolutionMarkdown: A man is treated as having no length — only the train's length counts.
